DOC.EP: EC.02.02.01 The hospital manages risks related to hazardous materials and waste. EP 1. The hospital maintains a written, current inventory of hazardous materials and waste that it uses, stores, or generates. The only materials that need to be included on the inventory are those who are handling, use, and storage is addressed by law and regulation. (See also IC.02.01.01, EP 6; MM.01.01.03, EP 3)
DOC.FINDING: The organization has not developed a complete list of hazardous waste at the facility. Review of documents and the Hazardous Materials and Waste program revealed that the organization has not identified pharmacy related wastes (including but not limited to, chemotherapeutic drugs and pharmaceuticals.).
DOC.RECOMMENDED: ? The organization must identify all hazardous wastes and construct a detailed list of types of wastes. ? The list should be provided for review in the program or other document.

DOC.EP: EC.02.03.05 The hospital maintains fire safety equipment and fire safety building features. Note: This standard does not require hospitals to have the types of fire safety equipment and building features described below. However, if these types of equipment or features exist within the building, then the following maintenance, testing, and inspection requirements apply. EP 1. At least quarterly, the hospital tests supervisory signal devices (except valve tamper switches). The completion date of the tests is documented. Note: For additional guidance on performing tests, see NFPA 72, 1999 edition (Table 7-3.2).
DOC.FINDING: During the review of fire component testing documents, documentation of quarterly testing for the fire pump was not provided. The organization has not tested and documented "pump on" and "failure".
DOC.RECOMMENDED: ? The organization must test and verify operational of supervisory signals at least quarterly. ? The fire pump supervisory signal must be tested and documented. EP 3. Every 12 months, the hospital tests duct detectors, electromechanical releasing devices, heat detectors, manual fire alarm boxes, and smoke detectors. The completion date of the tests is documented. Note: For additional guidance on performing tests, see NFPA 72, 1999 edition (Table 7-3.2).
DOC.FINDING: The organization tests all components. However, a detailed list of devices was not maintained.
DOC.RECOMMENDED: ? The organization should develop a complete inventory of tested devices.

DOC.EP: EC.02.04.03 The hospital inspects, tests, and maintains medical equipment. EP 1. Before initial use of medical equipment on the medical equipment inventory, the hospital performs safety, operational, and functional checks. (See also EC.02.04.01, EP 2)
DOC.FINDING: The hospital allows patient to bring in their own medical devices (such as C-PAP), but have no process for testing "patient owned equipment".
DOC.RECOMMENDED: ? The organization must develop a process for inspecting/testing patient owned equipment brought in to the facility. ? A policy defining the process must be developed.

DOC.EP: EC.02.05.01 The hospital manages risks associated with its utility systems. EP 2. The hospital maintains a written inventory of all operating components of utility systems or maintains a written inventory of selected operating components of utility systems based on risks for infection, occupant needs, and systems critical to patient care (including all life-support systems). The hospital evaluates new types of utility components before initial use to determine whether they should be included in the inventory. (See also EC.02.05.05, EPs 1, 3-5)
DOC.FINDING: The hospitals maintained a list of utility and developed PM schedule. The inventory and maintenance schedule was not developed by risk based criteria evaluations. The hospital EC plan for utilities states that risk criteria is used, but during the evaluation, the method of evaluation was not provided.
DOC.RECOMMENDED: ? The organization must develop risk based evaluation criteria before use of equipment. ? The evaluation must be conducted prior to use on all new equipment installed in the utility program

DOC.EP: EC.02.05.05 The hospital inspects, tests, and maintains utility systems. Note: At times, maintenance is performed by an external service. In these cases, hospitals are not required to possess maintenance documentation but must have access to such documentation during survey and as needed. EP 1. The hospital tests utility system components on the inventory before initial use. The completion date of the tests is documented. (See also EC.02.05.01, EP 2)
DOC.FINDING: The organization has installed a portable emergency generator. Observation of the generator revealed that battery warmers were not installed as required to provide reliable operation and starting (NFPA 110- for outdoor areas).
DOC.RECOMMENDED: ? The organization must install a battery warmer on battery assembly for the outdoor emergency generator.

DOC.EP: EC.02.05.09 The hospital inspects, tests, and maintains medical gas and vacuum systems. Note: This standard does not require hospitals to have the medical gas and vacuum systems discussed below. However, if a hospital has these types of systems, then the following inspection, testing, and maintenance requirements apply. EP 1. In time frames defined by the hospital, the hospital inspects, tests, and maintains critical components of piped medical gas systems, including master signal panels, area alarms, automatic pressure switches, shutoff valves, flexible connectors, and outlets. These activities are documented. (See also EC.02.05.01, EP 3)
DOC.FINDING: The hospitals policy did not define the testing frequency for oxygen/medical gas outlets and zone shut off valves. Testing records indicate that this testing was done periodically
DOC.RECOMMENDED: ? The organization must review NFPA 99 requirements and complete required testing as required. ? Testing frequency for all components of medical gas system must be defined in the organizations medical gas policy.

DOC.EP: EC.02.06.05 The hospital manages its environment during demolition, renovation, or new construction to reduce risk to those in the organization. EP 2. When planning for demolition, construction, or renovation, the hospital conducts a preconstruction risk assessment for air quality requirements, infection control, utility requirements, noise, vibration, and other hazards that affect care, treatment, and services. Note: See LS.01.02.01 for information on fire safety procedures to implement during construction or renovation.
DOC.FINDING: Review of one (1) construction project underway revealed that negative air was discontinued and that the ICRA was outdated. Review of one (1) construction project underway and in demo and rebuild stage revealed that negative air pressurization monitoring was not conducted. It was unclear if negative air was achieved.
DOC.RECOMMENDED: ? The organization must enhance it ICRA review process and monitoring. ? A current ICRA form must be in place for all projects. ? Negative air monitoring (manometers) must be in place to determine pressurization. ? Negative pressurization must be between 0.01 and 0.03 inches water ("H2O). EP 3. The hospital takes action based on its assessment to minimize risks during demolition, construction, or renovation.

DOC.EP: EC.04.01.01 The hospital collects information to monitor conditions in the environment. EP 15. Every 12 months, the hospital evaluates each environment of care management plan, including a review of the plan’s objectives, scope, performance, and effectiveness. (See also EC.01.01.01, EPs 3-8;

DOC.FINDING: Review of the annual evaluation of EC programs revealed that not all programs were evaluated for effectiveness and scope. The EC plans did not include performance indicators and quality improvement measures.
DOC.RECOMMENDED: ? The organization must develop a standard evaluation format and effectively report on each plans objectives, scope, performance, and effectiveness. ? The organization should list each plans performance indicators and quality improvement (PI- performance improvement) activities.
